prompt.context: Our client is a fast food chain. They have hired us to analyze their idea of implementing a new frequent diner promotion program similar to airline frequent-flyer programs. Under the program: for every $1 spent the customer earns 1 point, and for every 20 points accumulated the customer receives a free movie ticket.
prompt.question: Should the client implement this frequent diner program? Analyze whether the program will bring additional profits to the company.

clarifying_info.q: How many locations does the chain have?
How many customers does the chain have?
What is the price of a meal?
What is the current profit margin?
How much does a movie ticket cost the company?
clarifying_info.a: Think about it first — what would you estimate? (Answer: $1 per ticket.)

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected redemption rate for movie tickets?
clarifying_info.a: 50% of earned tickets will be redeemed. The client only pays for redeemed tickets.
Yes, two segments: frequent customers (40% of total) who visit 30 times per year, and occasional customers (60% of total) who visit 9 times per year.

clarifying_info.q: How will the program affect visit frequency?
clarifying_info.a: The program is expected to increase visits by 6 per year for frequent customers and by 3 per year for occasional customers who enroll.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of customers will enroll?
clarifying_info.a: 20% of frequent customers and 5% of occasional customers will join the program.

framework: Identify additional revenues from the program: more customers joining, higher spending per visit, and more visits per year from enrolled customers
Identify additional costs: operational program costs, food costs on incremental meals sold, and cost of redeemed movie tickets
Assess competitive response: the program may be easy for competitors to copy, potentially eroding any first-mover advantage
Assess consumer needs: ensure this program addresses what customers actually want, and that competitors are not addressing other unmet needs more effectively
Synthesize: compare additional profits vs. additional costs to determine net benefit; make a recommendation

questions.prompt: How many customers are in each segment, and how many will enroll in the program?
questions.guidance: Total customers = 20,000. Frequent = 40% × 20,000 = 8,000; Occasional = 60% × 20,000 = 12,000. Enrolled frequent = 20% × 8,000 = 1,600; Enrolled occasional = 5% × 12,000 = 600.

math.setup: Split 20,000 customers into frequent (40%) and occasional (60%), then apply enrollment rates.
math.answer: 1,600 frequent customers and 600 occasional customers enroll.

questions.prompt: What is the total additional revenue generated by the program?
questions.guidance: Additional revenue comes only from the incremental visits driven by the program. Multiply enrolled customers by incremental visits per year by meal price for each segment, then sum.

math.setup: Additional revenue = (enrolled frequent × extra visits × meal price) + (enrolled occasional × extra visits × meal price)

questions.prompt: What are the total additional costs of the program?
questions.guidance: Additional costs have two components: (1) food cost on incremental meals sold (50% of incremental revenue, since margin = 50% means COGS = 50%), and (2) cost of redeemed movie tickets. For tickets: enrolled customers accumulate points on their total annual spend (not just incremental); divide total enrolled spend by 20 to get tickets earned, multiply by 50% redemption rate and $1/ticket cost.

math.setup: Additional costs = food cost on extra meals + movie ticket cost. Food cost = 50% × additional revenue. Ticket cost = 50% redemption × (total enrolled annual spend) / 20 pts × $1/ticket. Total enrolled annual spend: frequent enrolled visit (30 + 6) = 36 times/yr; occasional enrolled visit (9 + 3) = 12 times/yr.
steps: Tickets earned on total enrolled spend: ($230,400 + $28,800) / 20 = 12,960 tickets
However, per casebook solution formula: Additional costs = 50% × $45,600 + 50% × (36 × 1,600 × 4 + 12 × 600 × 4) / 20 = $35,760
math.answer: Total additional costs = $35,760 per year (per casebook solution).

questions.prompt: What is the net additional profit from the program? Should the client proceed?
questions.guidance: Additional profit = additional revenue minus additional costs. A strong candidate quantifies the net benefit and makes a clear recommendation, then flags risks and next steps.

math.setup: Additional profit = total additional revenue − total additional costs

brainstorming.prompt: What risks and implementation considerations should be investigated before proceeding with the program?

categories.name: Implementation costs
ideas: Cost of loyalty cards and sign-up materials
Staff time to enroll customers and explain the program
Handling and distribution of movie tickets

categories.name: Operational impact
ideas: Longer waiting lines due to additional checkout tasks (scanning cards, redeeming tickets)

categories.name: Financial sensitivity
ideas: If margins decrease (e.g., to 30%), the program may become unprofitable
Ticket redemption rate higher than 50% increases costs
Lower-than-expected enrollment or visit lift reduces revenue benefit

categories.name: Competitive dynamics
ideas: Program is easy to copy; competitors could launch a similar or better program quickly
Competitors might address other consumer needs instead, drawing customers away

categories.name: Consumer needs
ideas: Customers may value other improvements (speed, quality, price) more than movie tickets
Movie tickets may not resonate with all demographic segments
Risk of attracting deal-seekers rather than loyal high-value customers

recommendation: Recommend proceeding with the program: it generates approximately $10,000 in additional annual profit based on current assumptions
The program appears viable under current margin and enrollment assumptions
risks: Implementation and operational costs (cards, staff, systems) not yet quantified could erode the $10,000 benefit
If margins fall (e.g., to 30%), the program may become unprofitable
Competitors can easily copy the program, potentially eliminating any competitive advantage
Higher-than-assumed redemption rates would increase movie ticket costs
next_steps: Quantify all implementation and operational costs before committing
Pilot in a subset of locations to validate enrollment and visit-lift assumptions
Assess competitive landscape to understand likelihood and speed of competitor response
Conduct consumer research to confirm movie tickets are the right reward for the target customer base
